suggestions.quote: The city lit up, built only from people we know
suggestions.fix: The city is a fourth new set after the hall, lane and stall, so it is the likeliest long pole. Build it as a pull-back from the same hall layers: the walls drift away and a skyline silhouette strip with glowing chips on four known heads replaces them. That needs no new set and keeps the 'this week' check safe.

suggestions.quote: the hall becomes one lit chair among two thousand five hundred
suggestions.fix: Draw the 2,500 as a procedural grid of small paper chairs with one lit, and run it as a camera pull-up from row three. Do not rig figures. Mark it as a code-drawn crowd so G2 does not read it as a new set.

suggestions.quote: chips flicker on over every head and yours glows crimson, 0.04%
suggestions.fix: Show numerals only on the key chips: yours, the cousin's, the teacher's, the topper's and the chaiwala's. Draw the other roughly 400 as unlabelled glows, so the text stays a split-flap counter and not a wall of small type. Put your chip where the thumbnail puts it (beside the head, on the pose from the thumbnail) so the first 7 s match the click.

suggestions.quote: his hand leaves the bat, and it rolls out of frame, then behind the cupboard
suggestions.fix: Time the wordless peak as four moves inside 8 to 10 s: the nod (about 2 s), the chip draining to grey (about 3 s), the hand opening (about 2 s), then the bat rolling and the cupboard cut (about 3 s). Each move lands on a 2 to 4 s change and no hold exceeds 6 s. At G2, cue the music drop on the chip draining or later, not on the nod. That is sound check #3.

suggestions.quote: the glowing chip over a head; it starts at the crowd's base rate and moves when that person acts
suggestions.fix: Settle colour continuity now. Chips glow warm white, yours is crimson, and the cousin's turns grey as it drains. Crimson is also the stranger's colour and the alarm colour, so name which head is the hidden stranger (suggest the man by the stall) so a crimson chip is not confused with him. Say who stays in colour: you, the stranger and the chips only.

Stage this as sound only over the hall, with no text. Keep the right third quiet for the last 15 s: you at the left, chips dimmed in the right third, no tag there. The end-card tags go in the left two thirds.

List what is reused and what is new. Reused: the night/lamp mood, the rigged you, the kid (cap) as the cousin, the boss-style tie figure for the teacher, the bubble and the split-flap counter. New: the cricket bat and cupboard, the chai stall, the hall chairs and desks, and the chip glyph. This lets G2 see that every new item is a small prop and not a set.

suggestions.quote: status: G1 awaiting the owner (batch 1, video 2 of 5)
suggestions.fix: `cues.yaml` is not in my inputs, and the SCENE, MOOD, HOLD, TAG and BUBBLE lines belong to the G2 script, so I could not judge the sound checks (#1 intent per beat, #3 music follows the story). At G2 the sheet needs a one-word intent per beat, with music in and out on named cues. The chip reveal and the 'Quit.' peak are the two reveals to guard.
